name: PREVIOUSLY IN GTM
tagline: A weekly read for founders, GTM leaders and growth marketers.
title: Every buying signal has a clock. Most teams never read it
standfirst: A long read on why the most valuable column in your signal list is the one almost nobody fills in: how long the buyer's window stays open.
cover_sub: The most valuable column in your signal list is the one almost nobody fills in.

insight.label: By the numbers
insight.text: to fix a cancelled insurance policy, with ten already gone by the time a trucking company's owner hears of it.
insight.source: Source: Cannonball GTM (Doug Bell), trucking example. Reported, not audited.

framework.title: Four questions for every buying signal
framework.subtitle: Ask them before a signal earns budget.
framework.footer: Rule of thumb (the author's own): window at least five times your reflex.

items.name: Threshold
items.question: When does it change the buyer's situation?
items.example: A cancelled policy does. A page visit rarely does.

items.name: Window
items.question: How long before the moment passes?
items.example: Hours, days or weeks, written down.

items.name: Reflex
items.question: How fast do you really answer?
items.example: Measured from signal to a human touch.

items.name: Owner
items.question: Who acts without asking?
items.example: One named person with authority to call.

news_cover.headline: Every buying signal has a clock: read it before you buy more
news_cover.deck: Four questions before a signal earns budget: Threshold, Window, Reflex, Owner.

alts.headline: Window minus reply time: the sum most signal lists fail
alts.deck: A signal is worth the window it opens, less the time you take to answer.

alts.headline: Time your front door before you buy another signal
alts.deck: Submit your own demo form and count the hours until a human replies.
